Translate one observed person into exactly three nesting-doll scales arranged together, with the largest doll preserving the clearest identity.
Show fine turned wood grain, a continuous horizontal shell seam and thin hand-painted facial and garment details.
Reuse identifying source hair, garment and accessory colors as restrained painted regions on warm wooden shells.
Use consistent soft studio illumination with believable contact shadows and modest satin varnish, never plastic toy gloss.
Repeat the same observed identity across the three scales; invent no extra person, text, jewelry or unrelated folk motifs.
Deliver one finished image at the input aspect ratio, without comparison panels, unrequested text, logos, signatures or watermarks.

preserve: Use one-person portraits only; intentionally create three decreasing dolls, replacing body anatomy with turned shells while preserving facial identity and clothing colors.
Preserve identifying features and required negative spaces, subject to the explicitly permitted transformation.
Keep the complete transformed subject within the input aspect ratio.
negative: Unrelated people, inconsistent identities, extra dolls beyond the three explicitly specified, detached shells or accidental clipping.
Unrequested titles, logos, signatures, watermarks, fabricated labels or before-and-after panels.
A generic filter without the requested medium-specific physical or optical mechanism.
